nary_nodes.label: Ebola treatment trial begins in DR Congo
evidence: A trial of potential treatments for the species of virus behind the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has begun, the World Health Organization (WHO) has announced.
The first patient has been enrolled in DR Congo, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Thursday.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
evidence: The current outbreak of Ebola in DR Congo began in May, though transmission had been going undetected for some time.
There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed cases in DR Congo
evidence: More than 1,400 cases and 438 deaths have been confirmed in the country, according to the WHO.
According to the WHO, 213 people have recovered.

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed cases in Uganda
evidence: There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed case in France
evidence: There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: WHO Director-General statement
evidence: Speaking to reporters from the WHO headquarters in Geneva on Thursday, Tedros said: 'Even without approved therapeutics, people are recovering from this disease, but of course, we could save many more lives with safe and effective therapeutics in our toolkit.'

nary_nodes.label: DR Congo Health Minister statement
evidence: DR Congo's Health Minister Dr Samuel Roger Kamba said the launch 'represents a significant step forward, offering renewed hope to patients, their families, and affected communities'.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola cases as of 1 July
evidence: According to the WHO, there have been 1,460 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with 150 suspected cases and 452 deaths, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola deaths as of 1 July
evidence: According to the WHO, there have been 1,460 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with 150 suspected cases and 452 deaths, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola recoveries as of 1 July
evidence: According to the WHO, 213 people have recovered.

nary_nodes.label: WHO declares public health emergency
evidence: The situation has been declared a public health emergency by the WHO.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola spreads through bodily fluids
evidence: It is spread through bodily fluids like blood.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola transmission from fruit bats
evidence: It normally infects animals, typically fruit bats, but outbreaks among humans can sometimes start when people handle infected animals.

nary_nodes.label: Outbreak restricted to eastern provinces
evidence: Congolese health authorities have said the outbreak is currently restricted to three eastern provinces - South Kivu, North Kivu and Ituri.

nary_nodes.label: Pregnant woman's body transported to Kisangani
evidence: The Reuters and AFP news agencies report that the body of a pregnant woman tested positive for Ebola in the neighbouring Tshopo province. The woman reportedly died in Ituri, before her body was transported by motorbike to Tshopo's main city, Kisangani, which has a population of about 1.5 million people.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola-positive individual fled to Haut-Uele
evidence: An individual suspected of having Ebola reportedly fled from an isolation unit in Ituri and later tested positive in the nearby Haut-Uele province.

nary_nodes.label: Contact-tracing efforts launched in Tshopo and Haut-Uele
evidence: Authorities are said to have launched contact-tracing efforts across Tshopo and Haut-Uele.

nary_nodes.label: Public gatherings banned in four provinces
evidence: Public gatherings were banned in both these provinces, along with neighbouring Bas-Uele and the capital, Kinshsasa, in order to prevent the spread of Ebola.

nary_nodes.label: Outbreak could be one of the largest ever
evidence: According to both Africa CDC and US public health authorities, the current outbreak has the potential to be one of the largest ever, because it was spreading for weeks before it was confirmed to be Ebola.
